title: Target Provisioning & Service Discovery: Metasploitable 2 TCP SYN Scan
summary: Provisioned an intentionally vulnerable target (Metasploitable 2) on the bridged local subnet (10.16.141.205), resolving virtual disk corruption and hypervisor configuration constraints (32-bit Ubuntu, IDE controller, single CPU). Verified Layer 3 connectivity from Kali Linux via ICMP echo (0% loss), followed by an active TCP SYN stealth service scan (nmap -sS -sV -T4). Discovered 22 open ports exposing high-risk legacy daemons including vsftpd 2.3.4, OpenSSH 4.7p1, Samba 3.x, UnrealIRCd, and an unauthenticated root bindshell on port 1524.

blocks.text: Before executing port scans, verified that the bridged virtual network adapter (`08:00:27:1D:80:01`) established bidirectional IP communication between Kali Linux and the Metasploitable 2 target at `10.16.141.205`.

rows: Contains a malicious smiley-face `:))` trigger that spawns a root shell on TCP 6200.
Legacy backdoor listening directly on port 1524 granting instant root privileges without credentials.
Arbitrary command execution via Samba user configuration vulnerability (CVE-2007-2447).
Backdoored IRC server allowing execution of arbitrary commands (CVE-2010-2075).
Hosts vulnerable web applications (Mutillidae, DVWA) and weak credential managers (`tomcat:tomcat`).

blocks.text: Unlike public cloud infrastructure where ingress traffic passes through reverse proxies (e.g. Cloudflare / Render), this internal target exposes bare daemons directly to Layer 4 probing.

items: Successfully resolved VM boot kernel panic by re-downloading uncorrupted media and aligning VirtualBox settings to 32-bit Linux / IDE / 1 CPU.
Established full Layer 2 / Layer 3 connectivity across Kali Linux and Metasploitable on `10.16.141.0/24`.
Identified 22 open services using `nmap` version scanning.
Prioritized high-severity targets for the next vulnerability assessment phase: vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor, Samba usermap script, and port 1524 bindshell.
